status_summary: The administration's main China trade tools have been the broad measures the essay argues against: Executive Order 14257 (signed 2025-04-02) set a baseline duty on all trading partners with country-specific rates, and later Section 232 and Section 301 actions apply to whole sectors or economies (see c26-02 and c26-04). Firm-level action has continued through export controls framed around national security rather than unfair trade practices: a BIS rule effective 2025-03-25 (90 FR 14046) added 11 Chinese entities and one in Taiwan to the Entity List for supporting military modernization through AI, chips and supercomputers, without citing intellectual property theft. A BIS interim final rule effective 2025-09-29 (90 FR 47201) extended Entity List restrictions to affiliates at least 50 percent owned by listed parties, and BIS suspended it on 2025-11-12 until 2026-11-09. A further firm-level measure, a DHS supply-chain security order published 2026-10-20 excluding DeepSeek products from civilian agency procurement, rests on the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act rather than on an unfair trade practice finding.

timeline.event: S. 330, the Combatting China's Pilfering of Intellectual Property Act, was introduced in the Senate and referred to the Foreign Relations Committee; it would require sanctions, including asset blocking and visa bars, on Chinese persons found to have engaged in a pattern of significant theft of U.S. intellectual property.
BIS added 12 entities (11 in China, 1 in Taiwan) to the Entity List, effective this date.
Executive Order 14257 (signed 2025-04-02) imposing a baseline and country-specific reciprocal tariff was published.
BIS published the Affiliates rule extending Entity List restrictions to 50 percent-owned affiliates.
BIS published a final rule suspending the affiliates rule for one year, until 2026-11-09 unless extended.

DHS publishes notice of a Secretary of Homeland Security order under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act (41 U.S.C. 1321 to 1328), issued after review of a Federal Acquisition Security Council recommendation, excluding information technology products and services of Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co. and its affiliates from federal civilian agency procurements and directing removal of DeepSeek-based products from civilian agency systems (91 FR 66346; filed for public inspection 2026-10-19; the signed order's date appears only in a scanned appendix).
